name: Machine Chest Fly
summary: A seated machine exercise that isolates the pectoralis major through horizontal adduction of the arms against guided resistance.

setup: Adjust the seat height so the handles or pads align with mid-to-lower chest level.
Sit back firmly against the pad with feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles or position forearms against the pads, maintaining a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
steps: Contract your chest to bring your hands together in an arc in front of your sternum.
Squeeze the chest muscles firmly at peak contraction for a brief pause.
Control the handles backward along the same arc until you feel a comfortable stretch across the pectorals.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you bring the handles together; inhale as you slowly return to the stretched starting position.
cues: Keep shoulders pinned back into the pad

common_faults.fault: Allowing the shoulders to shrug or roll forward at peak contraction.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulder blades retracted and depressed against the backrest throughout the rep.

common_faults.fault: Bending and extending the elbows excessively, turning the movement into a press.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a soft, locked elbow angle throughout the entire range of motion.

common_faults.fault: Overstretching the shoulder joint by allowing the arms to travel too far back.
common_faults.correction: Adjust the machine's starting range of motion so your elbows do not travel past the plane of your torso.

precautions: Use the machine's foot-release pedal if available to safely get into and out of the starting position.
